subject: MedFlow private footprint intake — runway & network checklist
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@medflow.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@medflow.io
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private footprint intake — initial network info

Hi Evelyn,

We're excited to kick off a Private deployment evaluation with Redwood. Before the intake call next week, can you share a concise list of the networking/account artifacts you need from us so we can assemble them? Specifically we want to be sure we have the right VPC/VNet info, egress IPs, any required load balancer details, and certificate/KMS expectations.

Attached is a very high-level network sketch to help start the conversation (MedFlow_NetTop_Level.pdf).

Targets from our side: we'd like the deployment to be available in our prod VPC, behind our firewall, and to keep data residency in us-west-2. Timeline is Q4 if everything lines up.

Can you also confirm the intake call attendees so we loop in our network/security folks?

Thanks —
Tom Reyes
Director, Infrastructure — MedFlow Health
ops@medflow.io
Attachment: MedFlow_NetTop_Level.pdf (high-level diagram, 1 page)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@medflow.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private footprint intake — initial network info

Tom — thanks for the note and the diagram, that helps. High level we generally need the following artifacts to progress the Private (VPC/on-prem) intake:

- VPC IDs and CIDR ranges for the target environment (prod/staging if both)
- NAT/egress IP addresses (for allowlists) and expected outbound volumes
- Firewall vendor + any existing permit rules we must align with
- Are you using PrivateLink or direct peering? If so, we need the peering config and reachable subnets
- KMS key ARN or HSM details for envelope encryption (if customer-managed)
- Service account / IAM role mapping and a list of engineers with deployment access
- Audit/logging retention requirements and any central SIEM endpoints
- If air-gapped/on-prem, a plan for artifact delivery and an estimate of available hardware (GPUs/CPU)

I'll attach our short intake checklist (see Drive link below) and proposed intake agenda. Proposed attendees from Redwood: myself (deployment lead), Ben Carter (onboarding engineer), Kimberly Park (security & KMS), Karthik Iyer (networking/ops).

Next steps: Can you share the VPC IDs and a contact from your network/security team (name and calendar availability)? I can lock an intake slot for Wed or Thu next week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Deployment Manager, Redwood Inference
Evelyn Hart | +1 415-555-0114
Redwood Inference
Related: https://drive.redwood/PrivDeploy/MedFlow/MAP-v1

Date: 2026-07-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: MedFlow intake - owner/action items

Eve / Kim / Karthik — looping to align owners before the external call. Quick proposed split:

- Ben: intake runbook, initial infra checklist, and scheduling the Day-0 access window
- Kimberly: KMS review, SOC 2 evidence mapping, and encryption policy confirmation
- Karthik: network validation (peering vs PrivateLink recommendations) and port allowlist

Questions I want answered on the call so we don't spin after:
1) Does MedFlow require outbound-only egress to our control plane or two-way peering for telemetry?
2) Any mandatory IP ranges for their egress appliances?
3) If they prefer a bastion/jump host model, confirm whether we supply the jumpbox AMI or they do.

I'll draft a tight mutual-action plan with milestones (30/60/90 days) to set expectations. If anyone has examples of special firewall vendor quirks (e.g., Palo Alto tag-based routing notes), drop them here.

- Ben
Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
